result.title: Effective Teacher Support for Reasoning Distillation
result.summary: Forward-KL language-model distillation normally computes dense teacher and student scores over the full vocabulary at every supervised position, making training and stored teacher targets expensive. We instead distill from the teacher's highest-probability vocabulary fraction, renormalizing the retained mass as we sweep support from 100% to 0.01%. Our main study distills Qwen3 4B -> 1.7B. We confirm the broader support-reduction finding on larger Qwen3 8B -> 4B and Nemotron Nano 12B -> 9B pairs and under answer-only supervision. We evaluate generation primarily on MMLU-Pro and secondarily on GPQA-Diamond. Across the Qwen3 settings, retaining 0.01% of the vocabulary causes no observed MMLU-Pro degradation relative to full-vocabulary distillation, although disagreement with the complete teacher distribution increases. Nemotron Nano matches full-vocabulary MMLU-Pro at 0.1%, but smaller fractions fail to emit the closing reasoning tag, showing that the reliable cutoff depends on the model family. At 0.01% support, caching the retained next-token scores from the teacher forward pass cuts training step time by 38%, while restricting student output computation to those tokens cuts peak memory by 24%; neither causes observed MMLU-Pro degradation.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文研究语言模型 forward-KL 蒸馏中只保留教师最高概率词表片段（从 100% 扫到 0.01%）并重新归一化的做法，在 Qwen3 与 Nemotron 多组师生对上验证精度影响，并结合教师分数缓存与受限输出计算降低训练时间与显存。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「稀疏教师支撑 + 缓存教师目标」的监督压缩思路，可能可供核查用于 latent/轨迹式推理蒸馏时监督信号成本与信息损失的权衡；但论文本身不涉及视觉或多模态状态，迁移属推测。
